newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up on last-gasp portfolio buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up on last-gasp portfolio buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended slightly higher Wednesday on last-minute buying for month-end portfolio valuation after drifting in negative ground for most of the pre-holiday session, traders said.
"It was a quiet session ... Volume was thin, dead." said Roberto Campuzano, an equity analyst with the Invex brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended up 5.48 points, or 0.14 percent, at 3,842.94.
Trading volume was lackluster at 51.2 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile ended up 4.53 points at 6,880.70 points.
Mexican financial markets are closed Thursday and Friday, March 27 and 28, for Easter. Many in Mexico have been on vacation since another public holiday was celebrated last Friday, March 21.
On the broad market, 98 shares changed hands, with gainers just outnumbering losers by 35 to 34.

Telmex L class weighed most heavily on the session, accounting for 23 percent of all shares traded, and ended down two centavos (less than one cent) at 15.66 pesos ($1.98). Telmex ADRs meanwhile closed down 1/8 at 39-3/8.
Dealers said last-minute buyers pushed up prices of holding company Grupo Carso, Carso Global Telecom and construction firm ICA.
Grupo Carso gained 50 centavos (6 cents) to 47.50 pesos ($6.01), Carso Global ended up 20 centavos ($2.53) at 24.50 ($3.10).
ICA meanwhile climbed 1.10 pesos (14 cents) to 130.00 pesos ($16.46).
Corn flour and tortilla maker Maseca was another prominent gainer, up 14 centavos (two cents) to 8.34 pesos ($1.06).
Radio network Radio Red said Wednesday morning the price ceiling for tortillas was to be raised by almost 50 percent, but the move was swiftly denied by the Mexican Trade Ministry.
Traders said the decliners' list was headed by stocks that had moved on low volume.
